authority_boundary: Classifications distinguish source-backed semantics from project engineering conventions. No market outcomes were inspected.

fields.current: Earlier H1/H4/D run context and remaining-run state may feed the 07:00 decision snapshot when legitimately knowable.
07:00 Asia/Bangkok is a preparation/assessment checkpoint, not an automatic order time.
Phase 1 waits for post-07:00 confirmation; current minimal lane uses completed M5 PAT2 confirmation.

Reference-execution convention is frozen pre-outcome: first archive tick strictly after confirmation known_at; BUY uses Ask and SELL uses Bid, marked REFERENCE_NOT_BROKER_FILL with slippage unmodeled. Exact broker fill remains unresolved.
Point-check/post-SIG destruction is structural invalidation; demonstrated SL references exist, but one universal exact stop/buffer is not source-closed.
Remaining inherited run is the source-backed objective. Exact position-closing mechanics at that objective are a replay convention.
Destroyed instance stops and re-evaluation/new SIG is source-backed; exact trade re-entry accounting is not universally fixed.
Captured Exness demo metadata is valid only for that environment; target runtime must be verified rather than hard-coded.

The frozen current Exness-branded archive snapshot has recorded Bid/Ask for 134/134 months classified AVAILABLE from 2015-08 through 2026-09. Validator V0.2 structural checks pass for all AVAILABLE months. Full every-tick continuity and exact equivalence to the current Exness Demo/MT5 feed are not established.

Per-row spread is derivable as Ask-Bid throughout the validated archive coverage and is already embedded in executable-side reference quotes. Historical broker fill slippage plus account-specific commission/fee/swap truth remain unresolved and block net economic proof; no zero-cost assumption is allowed.

When tick timestamps establish first touch, tick replay may resolve bar-level ordering. If conflicting stop/target or target/invalidation touches occur on distinct rows sharing the same timestamp, classify AMBIGUOUS_SAME_TIMESTAMP because source row order is not promoted to physical micro-order. Bar-only cases without finer data remain AMBIGUOUS_SAME_BAR.
Not required to study gross first-hit or per-trade R; required for account-level drawdown/cash outcome and supervised execution.
